Apex Industrial Technologies - Q3 FY2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Industrial Technologies Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star then 1 on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then 2. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Industrial Technologies' results for the Q3 FY2024. Joining me on today's call are Mark Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Jennifer Hayes, Chief Financial Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mark Reynolds.

Mark Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Apex Industrial Technologies' performance for the Q3. We've made significant progress on several fronts, and I'd like to highlight a few key achievements. We delivered robust organic revenue growth of 8%, complemented by inorganic contributions from recent acquisitions that added meaningful momentum. Order intake was strong with healthy book-to-bill trends, particularly in construction and mining, though agriculture faced some headwinds. Our automation and digital offerings continued to accelerate, driving efficiency gains for both us and our customers. We've executed thoughtfully on M&A, with bolt-on deals enhancing our positioning in high-growth areas. Capital expenditures are ramping strategically to support capacity and innovation. Macroeconomic factors have influenced demand variably across end markets, but our diversification provides resilience. We're progressing well on our share repurchase program, returning capital efficiently to shareholders. Finally, revenue performance was solid across regions, led by North America.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jennifer Hayes to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jennifer Hayes (CFO):
Thank you, Mark. Turning to our financial performance, Apex Industrial Technologies reported $2.48 billion in revenue for the quarter, representing a 12% increase year-over-year, or 11% on a constant currency basis. This exceeded our guidance midpoint and reflects the resilience of our core industrial equipment franchise amid a choppy macro environment. Gross margin expanded to 42%, driven by favorable product mix from high-margin automation and aftermarket services, pricing discipline, and supply chain optimizations. Operating expenses were $800 million, resulting in operating income of $450 million. Our net income for the quarter was $320 million, or $1.50 per share.

Let me break down the revenue growth into its organic and inorganic components, as this provides the clearest lens into our execution and strategy. Starting with organic revenue growth, which excludes acquisitions, FX, and divestitures, we achieved a robust 8% increase. This stemmed from volume expansion, modest pricing, and strength in key end markets. In our Machinery segment, including CNC machining centers, stamping presses, and heavy fabrication equipment, we saw 7% organic growth, driven by 10% higher bookings from OEMs in automotive and aerospace—like Tier-1 suppliers for EV platforms and Boeing's 737 MAX ramp. Our Automation & Robotics division surged 15% organically, riding Industry 4.0 waves with customers like Ford and Tesla deploying collaborative robots and AI palletizers. Aftermarket services and MRO, at 45% of revenues and our highest-margin area, grew 9%, bolstered by our predictive maintenance platform using digital twins and edge computing across over 50,000 connected assets.

Regionally, North America led with 10% organic growth, boosted by Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act tailwinds in data centers and reshoring—U.S. semi-fab demand lifted precision tooling by 12%, similar to Applied Materials' ecosystem. EMEA grew 6%, with offshore wind projects driving hydraulic systems and turbine components, despite German auto softness. APAC hit 7%, aided by China's post-COVID rebound in solar PV equipment, gaining share versus Fanuc and Yaskawa. Underpinning this was a 22% backlog build to $4.2 billion from multi-year capex in electrification and automation. Pricing added 2 points, covering 85% of raw material inflation, while R&D up 18% YoY to $120 million yielded wins like our ApexForge 5.0 CNC series with generative AI, securing $250 million in design wins, cutting lead times 30%, and boosting yields.

Inorganic contributions from acquisitions added 4 points to the total 12% growth, aligned with our bolt-on plus platform strategy for megatrends like sustainability and digitalization. The March Precision Dynamics Robotics acquisition, a UK cobot specialist for battery gigafactories at $450 million, added $85 million or 3.5 points, with 20% EBITDA margins from cross-selling our servo motors. Synergies are ahead at $15 million annualized via supply chain and shared R&D. The Q1 RoboForge Solutions tuck-in, focused on additive manufacturing for aerospace MRO, contributed $22 million or 0.9 points, targeting the $50 billion AM market as airlines extend overhauls. Collectively, these expand our addressable market 15%, with pro forma inorganic at 25% CAGR since 2022.

Shifting to revenue by geographic region, we saw balanced strength. North America, 45% of revenue at $1.12 billion, grew 18% YoY and 7% sequentially, powered by CHIPS Act and EV onshoring—wins for FANUC-compatible robotic welders at Intel Ohio and GM Michigan. Aftermarket up 25% via EdgeConnect IoT, expanding margins 250bps to 28%. Europe, 25% or $620 million, rose 8% YoY, led by energy-efficient palletizers for Vestas under EU Green Deal, offsetting auto destocking; our Siemens JV cobots added $45 million. Asia-Pacific, 20% or $496 million, increased 5%, with China at 2% but India/SE Asia up 35% on PLI incentives for Tata and Samsung robots. Rest of World, 10% or $248 million, grew 15%, driven by LATAM nearshoring and Middle East LNG.

On M&A, year-to-date we've deployed $1.2 billion, 25% of capex/buyback budget, at 9.2x EV/EBITDA—below our 11.5x historical. Q3 highlights: $650 million RoboForge Technologies for cobots and AI tending, adding $180 million revenue at 22% margins, accretive via ForgeAI integration with our Nexus IoT; $25 million synergies from supply chain, APAC boost, and U.S. semi redirection. And $550 million EuroPress Hydraulics for electro-hydraulic presses, $130 million revenue at 19% margins, enabling 40% energy savings for Volvo/ZF; $35 million synergies, targeting offshore wind. Pipeline includes ASEAN tooling and digital twins software, targeting 10-12% CAGR inorganic.

For capital expenditures, we're guiding $450 million for FY2024, up 15% from 2023, focused on capacity, digital, and sustainability. 40% or $180 million to manufacturing: $75 million Greenville, SC greenfield for hydraulic presses serving Magna/Lear EV ramp; $40 million Dortmund modernization for wind components; Shanghai JV for battery coaters. 30% or $135 million to digital: 500 cobots for 18-20% productivity lift, $50 million AI predictive maintenance cutting downtime 35%, digital twins shortening cycles. 20% or $90 million to sustainability: solar microgrids, electric fleet, EcoForge hydrogen presses. Balance to maintenance. ROIC >15%, funded 65% from $320 million H1 OCF.

Regarding macro factors impacting end markets, global GDP at 2.8%, ISM PMI 47.2, high rates, and supply frictions pressured OEM bookings down 12%, offset by 15% aftermarket. Aerospace/defense down 18% on Boeing stalls; auto/EV up 8% on gigafactories; oil/gas +12% on Permian/LNG; semis flat; general industrial/mining -15%. North America +2%, EMEA -14%, APAC -10%. We're countering with Machinery 4.0 IoT/digital twins for 12% uptime gains, inventory trough nearing, pricing covering inflation.

On share repurchases, under $1.0 billion authorization, we've executed $420 million, 8.4 million shares at $50.12 average, reducing share count 3.8%. Opportunistic via 10b5-1 and blocks, accelerating in Q3 dips. Funded by $650 million YTD FCF from $4.2 billion backlog; $580 million remains. Accretes $0.28 EPS YTD.

We remain committed to disciplined capital allocation and maximizing shareholder value.

Now, I will hand over to Robert Kline, COO, for an operational update.

Robert Kline (COO):
Thank you, Jennifer. Operationally, we've been focused on optimizing our manufacturing processes, improving supply chain efficiency, and enhancing our customer service capabilities. Total order intake hit $2.85 billion, up 12% YoY and 5% sequentially, with aftermarket at 28% mix; trailing book-to-bill 1.12x, backlog $14.2 billion up 8%.

By end market: Construction (42% orders, $1.2 billion) surged 22% YoY, book-to-bill 1.25x; NA +28% on IIJA for excavators/loaders, Gen-5 electrics 15% mix; EMEA +10%, APAC +18%. Mining (18%, $510 million) +8%, 1.08x; NA +15% ultra-haul trucks, autonomous 10%; LATAM +5%, APAC flat but electrics +30%. Agriculture (12%, $340 million) -5%, 0.92x on low commodities; NA -8%, EMEA +2%, but autonomy +18%; idled capacity redirected.

Overall, NA orders +15%, EMEA 6%, APAC 8%; tech like 48V hybrids 22% intake. Book-to-bill supports 10-12% organic FY24. We're leveraging digital technologies and data analytics to drive operational excellence. We're also focused on ensuring the health and safety of our employees.

And I will turn the call over to our CTO, Dr. Elena Vasquez, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Elena Vasquez (CTO):
Thank you, Robert. We are committed to driving innovation and developing cutting-edge solutions for our customers. Automation and digital revenues hit $285 million, +28% YoY, 12% sequential, 22% of segment (up from 17%); orders +35%, book-to-bill 1.28x; recurring SaaS $128 million +42%, ARR $520 million; digital margins 72%, +150bps overall.

IntelliForge IIoT at 1,200 sites cuts downtime 18-22%, e.g., steel fabricator +25% OEE. Cobot cells +15% throughput. NA +40% on CHIPS, EMEA +32% Green Deal, APAC +25% India/SE Asia. Pillars: $450 million R&D +20% for gen AI prescriptive maintenance; Rockwell/NVIDIA lab for vision; outcome pricing, +15% wins. Scaling to 28% revenues, 30%+ growth, 65% inc margins.

We're investing in R&D in AI, ML, robotics, IoT for predictive maintenance, operations optimization. Our new ApexForge 5.0 is significantly impacting the market, with design wins accelerating adoption and efficiency.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Ben Harris with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Harris (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you discuss the long-term impact of the new ApexForge 5.0 on your revenue and profitability?

Dr. Elena Vasquez (CTO):
Thanks, Ben. The ApexForge 5.0 with integrated generative AI for adaptive machining is a game-changer, shortening lead times 30% and improving yields, as seen in $250 million design wins. Long-term, it drives recurring digital services via IoT data streams, targeting 72% margins. We expect it to contribute mid-teens percentage points to automation growth, scaling our high-margin digital mix to 28% of revenues by year-end, supporting 12-15% EPS expansion through efficiency multipliers and premium pricing in EV and semi markets.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for revenue growth in the coming year?

Jennifer Hayes (CFO):
Good question, Sarah. For FY2025, we guide 10-12% organic revenue growth, mid-teens total including inorganic from pipeline M&A. Q4 organic 7-9%, with backlog visibility at $14.2 billion and book-to-bill 1.12x providing confidence. Tailwinds from NA reshoring, construction infra, mining electrification offset ag softness; digital at 30%+ growth. FCF conversion elite at 110% funds it all.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel (Morgan Stanley):
Can you discuss your plans for expanding your global footprint?

Mark Reynolds (CEO):
Absolutely, Mike. We're prioritizing reshoring and diversification: $450 million CapEx includes Greenville and Shanghai expansions, Dortmund modernization. M&A like EuroPress boosts EMEA, RoboForge APAC; targeting ASEAN EV and India PLI. Reducing China to 11%, growing NA to 50%, with localized manufacturing cutting lead times 20%. Digital twins and JVs like Siemens enable this, aiming 20% CAGR in emerging markets.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong (Barclays):
How are you managing rising energy costs?

Robert Kline (COO):
Thanks, Lisa. Energy costs up amid volatility, but we're proactive: $90 million CapEx for solar microgrids targeting 25% Scope 1 cuts, electric forklifts, low-emission coaters for AB32/CBAM compliance. Gen-5 electrics and ePress servos save 40% vs. traditional hydraulics. IntelliForge pilots yield 20% savings, as with Konecranes OEMs. Supply chain localization covers 85% inflation pass-through, maintaining margins.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Closing Remarks:

Mark Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Industrial Technologies. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Emily Carter (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
